samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small notice board made of six separated tiles: three tiles in an upper row and three tiles in a lower row, with plain background between every tile. The leftmost tile of the upper row is the badge: one coloured square drawn inside a thin dark rectangular ring, and its colour is the colour carried at the start. Each of the other five tiles is a card: two coloured squares side by side at the same height with a background gap between them, the left square being that card's guard colour and the right square being that card's result colour. Every square is red, green, blue, purple or orange. The cards act one after another in reading order: first the two cards to the right of the badge in the upper row, left to right, then the three cards of the lower row, left to right. When a card acts, compare the colour carried at that moment with that card's guard colour: if they are the same colour, the carried colour becomes that card's result colour; if they are not the same colour, that card does nothing at all and the carried colour is unchanged. The board may sit anywhere on the canvas, and every grey mark outside the board is inert decoration. Which colour is carried after the last card has acted? Answer with one of red, green, blue, purple or orange.
